sentences.text: Zosuchus is a basal crocodyliform genus from the Late Cretaceous period found in Mongolia. It possessed a very short snout.

The fossil was discovered in the Redbeds of Zos Canyon in the Gobi Desert by the American Museum of Natural History and described by Diego Pol and Mark Norell in 2004. The only known species, Z. davidsoni, was named in honor of preparator Amy Davidson. The fossil record consists of five specimens, including a holotype with an isolated skull and lower jaws.
Zosuchus is considered a terrestrial crocodyliform, distinct from modern crocodiles.
A 2018 analysis placed Zosuchus within the basal mesoeucrocodyliform clade Shartegosuchoidea. Zosuchus belongs to the suborder Protosuchia within the order Crocodyliformes.

Zosuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous period in the Redbeds of Zos Canyon within the Djadochta Formation of the Gobi Desert in Mongolia. It lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
